About Bennett Contracting

Bennett Contracting is a full-service remodeling contractor dedicated to providing the highest level of service and craftsmanship to help improve existing homes and businesses in the Capital Region. With over 80 employees including carpenters, plumbers, electricians, designers, and office staff, we are prepared to help plan and design any remodeling project.

Founded in 1915 by Dan Bennett in Delmar, New York, the company evolved over 100 years from a small plumbing company to a full-service remodeling contractor. Dan’s sons-in-law grew the plumbing business into DA Bennett Heating & AC following WWII. One of Dan’s grandson’s, Greg Jackson, and childhood friend, Paul Gutman, established the DA Bennett Insulation division in the late 1970s. This division eventually broke off into its own company called Bennett Contracting, Inc. in 1984, and was led by Greg and Paul for over 40 years.

In 2019, Andrew Gutman and Kevin Gutman took over as the owners of Bennett Contracting. This transition plan was developed to ensure that the company is safely on its way to a second one hundred years in business. Firsthand involvement by the owners ensures that Bennett’s high standards are passed on to every customer on every project.

From kitchens and bathrooms to additions, windows, doors, siding, and outdoor living spaces, we help improve the comfort, function, and longevity of existing homes. Our approach is practical, collaborative, and grounded in how people actually live in their spaces.

Our Capital Region home remodeling services include:

The replacement of Windows, Doors and Siding
The design and renovation of Kitchens, Bathrooms and Basements
The design and building of Home Additions
The design and installation or renovation of Decks, Porches or Seasonal Rooms

We believe great remodeling is built on trust—and that trust is earned by doing what we say we’ll do, showing up when we say we will, and standing behind our work.

Our Purpose

At Bennett Contracting, our purpose is to serve our customers and employees with integrity and care, and to improve homes and uphold a century-long commitment to our community through exceptional craftsmanship.

Our Vision

To be the Capital Region’s most trusted name in home remodeling: where craftsmanship meets care, and every project begins a lasting relationship.

Our Mission

We transform houses into homes through expert design, quality construction, and personal service. With a hands-on approach and a collaborative mindset, we provide solutions and guide our clients through every step of the remodeling journey, delivering spaces they’re proud to live in and eager to share. We support our employees with a culture of teamwork, growth, and pride in our shared legacy.

Our Values

Since 1915, Bennett Contracting has been guided by values that shape how we work today.

Trust
We’ve earned our reputation over generations by doing what we say we’ll do, when we say we’ll do it.

Reliability
We offer dependability, stability and consistency to our customers and coworkers.

Uncompromised Quality
We hold ourselves to the highest standards of quality, from the jobsite to the office.

Service
We prioritize people-our customers, coworkers, and community-above all else.

Teamwork
We believe the best work happens together. Every voice matters, and every contribution counts.

Embrace Progress
We learn from experience, encourage new ideas, and strive to constantly innovate how the business operates to stay ahead of the industry.

Do the Right Thing
Honesty and integrity serve as the foundation of how we do business and treat our coworkers.

Family Owned and Operated

Bennett Contracting entered its fourth generation as a family-owned business in 2019. Brothers Andrew and Kevin Gutman assumed ownership following decades of leadership by Greg Jackson and Paul Gutman.

Today, Andrew and Kevin remain actively involved in day-to-day operations, ensuring Bennett’s standards for quality, reliability, and safety are upheld on every project.

Professional, Responsive, and Local

Strong communication is a key part of a successful remodeling experience. From our fully staffed home office and showroom at 693 S. Pearl Street in Albany, NY, customers can always reach a knowledgeable professional for timely answers and reliable support.
See all the communities we serve.

Just as important are the people behind the work. From our experienced office staff to our skilled carpenters and craftsmen in the field, Bennett’s team brings professionalism, coordination, and care to every project. That consistency—across design, construction, and communication—is a key reason homeowners continue to choose Bennett and refer us to others.
Meet our team.

Safety Is a Core Standard

Safety is fundamental to how Bennett operates. Protecting our employees, our customers, and the homes we work in is a responsibility we take seriously on every project.

That commitment is reinforced through regular safety meetings, ongoing training, and our annual Safety Fest, where teams come together for hands-on education and shared learning around best practices on the jobsite. Our approach to safety has also earned industry recognition, including national awards for safety programming from the National Association of Home Builders. 

While we’re proud of that recognition, what matters most is the day-to-day culture behind it; organized jobsites, consistent workmanship, and accountability at every level.

100 Year History
Reliability. Trust. Quality. Value.

These are the ideas on which Bennett Contracting was first founded in 1915. As a third generation family run house contractor business based in Albany, NY, we are proud to stand behind the belief that every project, no matter how big or small, deserves our utmost attention and care. What began as a small plumbing business has currently expanded to a substantial company with a fleet of over 35 cars, trucks and trailers and 70 full-time professional employees.

Company Timeline

1915:  Dan (D.A.) Bennett opens a plumbing shop in a rented garage in Delmar, NY.

“Dan learned his trade as a steam fitter on the railroad.  In 1915 indoor plumbing and central heat were a “new thing” and he was able to take his skills and move into this new industry.  Things were simpler then, workers paid in cash at the end of the day and contracts written on the back of old envelopes.” 

-Greg Jackson, Co-Founder Bennett Contracting.

 

1945:  Dan’s sons-in-law Gill and Bud return form WWII and join the company, which becomes DA Bennett Plumbing & Heating.  The company enjoys strong post war growth along with the Bethlehem community.

 

1976:  Gil’s son Tom joins the company and at the suggestion of long time friend Paul Gutman starts an insulation business.  Greg Jackson, another grandson, joins to run the new insulation company, DA Bennett Insulation Company.

 

1978:  Paul Gutman join Greg Jackson as co-owners of the DA Bennett Insulation Company.

“At the time we started the insulation business we did less work in a year than we do now in a week.  Our office was a warehouse our office walls were bags on insulation.  We shared a double desk and single rotary phone, if you needed a photo copy you took a dime and went to the library.”  

-Greg Jackson, Co-Founder Bennett Contracting.

 

1984:  Paul and Greg become the sole owners of the newly named Bennett Contracting, Inc.  They move the business to their current location at 693 S Pearl St in Albany, NY.

“During these years the company came of age and grew from 10 employees to over 70 today.  It expanded beyond insulation into a full-service remodeling firm, with the development of our insurance, commercial, and home remodeling services.  Our kitchen and bath business increased 1000%.  We have since added adjacent land and built offices, showroom and warehousing.” 

-Paul Gutman, Co-Founder Bennett Contracting.

 

1990’s & 2000’s: The business grows and expands into new products and services. Beyond just windows and insulation, the company enters into residential general contracting and commercial renovations. The office and field staff increase to around 50 employees by 2010.

 

2010: Ground is broken on Bennett Contracting’s first major office expansion. A 3-story addition is added, providing space for a new showroom, more offices and meeting space in the basement.

 

2016: Bennett’s evolution leads to bringing design in house. Our first designer, Justina Auer, joins the team and Bennett becomes a dealer of cabinets and countertops in order to support to support their robust remodeling projects. This allows for Project Manager to take full control of the projects from start to finish, without the need for relying on third parties.

 

2019: Andrew and Kevin Gutman purchase the business from Paul Gutman and Greg Jackson, entering its fourth generation of ownership for the Bennett brand. The company stands at about 75 employees and has garnered an exceptional reputation in the region for home renovations.

“We are committed to continue our 100 plus year tradition of quality and integrity in the remodeling and renovation business.  Dedicating ourselves to the success of our employees and the service of our customers, neighbors, and friends.”

-Andrew Gutman, President Bennett Contracting.

Remodeling Projects in Albany & the Capital Region

Bennett Contracting is a full-service home remodeling contractor serving Albany and the greater Capital Region. For more than 100 years, we’ve helped homeowners update the rooms they live in every day, improve comfort and efficiency, and protect the long-term value of their homes.

This page is a guide to the most common project types we build: from kitchen remodeling and bathroom renovations to replacement windows and doors, siding, decks and porches, and home additions. If you’re not sure where to start, that’s normal. Most great projects begin with a simple question: What would make your home work better for you right now?

Our team is built for clarity. We don’t do high-pressure, commission-driven sales. We offer no-pressure consultations led by experienced professionals, so you can make the right decision for your home, on your timeline.

Kitchens | Bathrooms | Windows | Doors | Siding | Decks & Porches | Additions | FAQs

Explore Our Remodeling Services
Window Replacement & Installation

Drafty frames, fogged panes, and windows that no longer insulate the way they should are common across older homes in the Capital Region. Bennett installs high-performance replacement windows designed for comfort, durability, and clean architectural fit — whether you’re upgrading a historic Albany property or a newer suburban home. We help you compare materials, understand energy performance, and choose options that make sense for your home and your budget.

Our approach is straightforward and professional. Openings are protected, installations are precise, and your home is respected throughout the process. Estimates are guided by experienced professionals — not commission-based sales tactics — so you can make the right decision without pressure.

Explore Window Replacement Services

Not sure what you need? Schedule a no-pressure consultation

Exterior & Entry Door Installation

Exterior doors shape first impressions, protect against Upstate weather, and play a critical role in efficiency and security. Bennett installs entry doors, patio doors, and specialty exterior doors with careful attention to structure, insulation, and finish details. We walk you through material and performance options so you understand the long-term impact before moving forward.

From initial assessment to final trim work, our installations are handled with discipline and clarity. We explain the scope, protect the opening properly, and execute with care — ensuring the door looks right, seals properly, and performs reliably through every season.

Explore Door Installation Services

Not sure what you need? Schedule a no-pressure consultation

Bathroom Remodeling

A bathroom remodel should do two things at once: make daily routines easier, and make the room feel like it finally fits the home. Bennett’s bathroom remodeling team handles full renovations — not quick cover-ups — with the plumbing, electrical, tile, and finish work required to get it right.

Whether you’re updating a primary bath, improving a guest bath, or planning for aging-in-place comfort, we help you make smart choices that balance durability, maintenance, and design. Good bathrooms aren’t built from trends. They’re built from details: ventilation that actually works, waterproofing you don’t have to think about, storage that’s intentional, and finishes that feel clean and lasting.

Our process is designed to reduce stress. We’ll talk through scope early, outline realistic timelines, and communicate clearly as the project moves from design to build.

Explore Bathroom Remodeling

Read: How Long a Bathroom Remodel Takes | Project Highlight: Bathroom Remodel in Loudonville

Kitchen Remodeling

Kitchens are where homes reveal their real habits. Who cooks. Who hosts. Who drops backpacks on the same corner every day. A successful kitchen remodel improves workflow and storage without losing the character of the home, especially in older Capital Region properties where “simple updates” often uncover hidden complexities.

Bennett provides full-service kitchen remodeling, including design guidance, layout updates, cabinetry and countertop coordination, lighting, flooring, and finish carpentry. Whether you’re opening sightlines, improving storage, or building a kitchen that finally feels like it belongs in the home, our team manages the details that make the difference: transitions, clearances, trim, and the small functional decisions you’ll live with for years.

If you’re deciding between a light refresh and a full renovation, we’ll help you weigh value, timeline, and disruption – with honest guidance, not pressure.

Explore Kitchen Remodeling

Read: Kitchen Remodel Budget Considerations (Capital Region) | Project Highlight: An Inviting Kitchen Remodel

Decks & Porches

Outdoor projects are where function meets seasonality. A deck or porch should feel like a natural extension of the home: built to handle Northeast weather, daily use, and the kind of summer you actually want to have.

Bennett designs and builds decks and porches that prioritize structure and longevity first, then finishes. That means thoughtful framing, clean connections to the home, and material choices that make sense for your maintenance preferences (natural wood vs composite, covered vs open-air, screened vs fully exposed). We also help homeowners plan early enough to align design decisions with build schedules, because outdoor timelines fill up fast.

If you’re thinking “we want something simple,” we’ll translate that into scope you can trust — the kind that doesn’t surprise you halfway through.

Explore Decks & Porches

Read: 5 Signs You Might Need a New Deck | Project Highlight: A Delightful Deck in Clifton Park

Siding Installation

Siding is one of those projects that’s easy to underestimate — until you see what it changes. Done well, siding improves curb appeal, reduces maintenance, protects the building envelope, and can solve real problems like moisture intrusion or persistent drafts.

Bennett installs siding with a builder’s mindset. We look at what’s happening underneath: trim, flashing, corner details, and how water moves across the exterior. Then we recommend a solution that fits your home, your neighborhood, and your long-term maintenance preferences. This matters even more in Upstate conditions, where freeze-thaw cycles and older construction can expose weaknesses over time.

If you’re comparing options (materials, profiles, color, insulation), we’ll walk you through tradeoffs clearly — and help you make a decision you won’t regret five years from now.

Explore Siding Services

Read: 4 Myths About Vinyl Siding | Project Highlight: New Siding on a Modern Home

Additions & Whole-Home Remodeling

Some homes don’t need a single-room fix. They need a new plan. Additions and whole-home remodels are about creating space that fits the next phase of life, whether that means a new primary suite, expanded kitchen footprint, a better mudroom entry, or a multi-room reconfiguration that finally makes the home flow.

These projects require more than good carpentry. They require project management, coordination, and clear communication because the scope touches structure, mechanicals, permits, and schedule sequencing. Bennett’s team is built for that complexity. We manage the process with discipline and guide decisions early to keep the build stage predictable.

If you’re exploring a bigger vision but want a grounded path forward, this is where a no-pressure consult helps most: we can discuss feasibility, budget ranges, and next steps without locking you into anything.

Explore Additions & Remodeling
Not Sure Where to Start? Choose the Right Project Type

If you’re debating where to invest first, start with what’s most “structural” to your daily comfort.

If your home feels drafty or loud: windows and doors often deliver the fastest comfort upgrade.
If daily routines feel cramped: kitchens and bathrooms typically have the biggest lifestyle impact.
If the exterior looks tired or maintenance-heavy: siding can change both appearance and protection.
If you’ve outgrown the layout: additions and reconfigurations create long-term solutions.

The best next step isn’t guessing. It’s a conversation. We’ll help you prioritize based on your home, your goals, and your timeline – without pressure.

Talk to an expert
The Bennett Difference

No-pressure. Expert-led. Built to last.

Bennett is not a high-pressure, commission-based sales organization. Our consultations are guided by experienced professionals who focus on the right solution, not a quick close.

What that means for you:

Clear scope, early. We define what’s included (and what isn’t) before work begins.
Process you can follow. You’ll know what happens next, and why.
Craft you live with. We treat finish details like they matter. Because they do.
A century of reputation. Trust is earned in the long run. We’ve been doing that since 1915.
FAQs
What areas do you serve?

We serve homeowners across Albany, Saratoga, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Fulton, and Montgomery Counties, with select projects in Columbia and Greene Counties depending on service type and schedule.

Do you offer no-pressure estimates?

Yes. Our process is built for clarity, not pressure. We’ll walk through your goals, evaluate your home, and provide an honest recommendation and estimate — without “today only” tactics.

How long does a remodel take?

Timelines depend on scope, selections, and scheduling. A window or door replacement may be completed quickly, while kitchens, bathrooms, and additions require more planning and build time. We’ll outline expected milestones before construction begins.

How much will my project cost?

Costs vary based on scope, materials, and site conditions. We’ll give you a clear estimate after discussing your goals and evaluating the space. If you’re early in planning, we can also walk you through the main cost drivers so you know what to expect.

Will I need permits?

Many projects require permits depending on scope and municipality. We’ll advise you early and handle permitting steps as part of the process when required.

Do you offer financing?

Yes. Bennett Contracting offers financing options through a trusted lending partner to help make larger projects more manageable. We view financing as a convenience — not a sales tool — and we’re happy to walk you through available options if it helps align your project timing with your budget.

Ready to plan a project you’ll feel good about for years?

Whether you know exactly what you want, or you’re still figuring it out, we’ll help you find the right path forward.

Why Choose Bennett for Remodeling & Additions?

Large remodeling and addition projects require more than skilled carpentry. They demand coordination, foresight, and steady project management over weeks or months of work.

Homeowners trust Bennett because we offer:

A full-service remodeling and construction team
Experienced project managers overseeing every phase

Our approach is straightforward and professional. We don’t rely on high-pressure sales tactics. We focus on helping homeowners understand their options, make informed decisions, and move through complex projects with confidence.

What We Mean by “Remodeling & Home Additions”

Remodeling and additions cover a wide range of projects that go beyond single-room updates. These projects often involve structural changes, multi-room coordination, and long-term planning.

Whole-Home & Multi-Room Remodeling

For homeowners updating multiple spaces at once, we coordinate design, construction, and sequencing to ensure the work is cohesive and efficient. This may include kitchens, bathrooms, living areas, and circulation spaces—planned together, not in isolation.

Structural Changes & Reconfiguration

Many older homes were built for different lifestyles than today’s. Remodeling may involve removing or relocating walls, improving flow, reinforcing structure, or updating layouts to better support modern living.

Home Additions

When more space is needed, a home addition can expand living areas without sacrificing the character of your home. Common projects include primary suite additions, family rooms, in-law spaces, and expanded kitchens or living areas. Our goal is to make new construction feel intentional and integrated—not like an afterthought.

Common Reasons Homeowners Remodel or Add On

Homeowners throughout the Capital Region choose remodeling and additions for many reasons, including:

Outgrowing an existing layout
Adapting a home for long-term living or aging in place
Improving functionality in older homes
Creating space for extended family or guests
Preserving a location or neighborhood they love

These projects are often deeply personal and carefully considered. Our role is to help homeowners evaluate options and move forward with clarity.

Our Remodeling & Addition Process

A clear process is essential for larger-scale projects. Bennett’s approach is designed to reduce uncertainty and keep projects moving smoothly.

Initial Conversation & Evaluation

We begin by learning about your goals, your home, and the scope of work you’re considering. This early phase helps determine feasibility, priorities, and next steps.

Design & Planning

For projects requiring design, layouts, or structural planning, we collaborate with designers and engineers as needed. This phase allows details to be resolved before construction begins.

Pre-Construction & Permitting

We help guide homeowners through permitting requirements and scheduling. This stage ensures the project is properly prepared and compliant with local codes before work starts.

Construction & Project Management

During construction, our project managers coordinate trades, materials, and timelines. Communication remains consistent so homeowners know what to expect as work progresses.

Completion & Walkthrough

Once construction is complete, we review the finished work together, address final details, and ensure everything meets expectations.

Frequently Asked Questions About Remodeling & Home Additions
How long does a remodeling or home addition project take?

Timelines vary depending on scope, complexity, and permitting. Smaller remodels may take several weeks, while larger projects or additions can take several months. A realistic timeline is established during planning so expectations are clear before construction begins.

Do I need permits for a home addition or major remodel in New York?

Most remodeling and addition projects that affect structure, layout, or footprint require permits. Local requirements vary by municipality. Bennett helps homeowners navigate the permitting process and ensures work complies with applicable building codes.

Can I live in my home during remodeling or addition work?

In many cases, yes—but it depends on the scope of the project. Some homeowners remain in their homes during construction, while others choose temporary relocation for comfort or safety. This is discussed early so homeowners can plan accordingly.

How are remodeling and addition projects planned and sequenced?

Larger projects are broken into phases to maintain order and minimize disruption. Design, permitting, and pre-construction planning happen first, followed by carefully scheduled construction stages. Clear sequencing helps keep projects efficient and predictable.

How do you protect existing living areas during construction?

We take steps to limit disruption, including isolating work zones, protecting surfaces, and maintaining safe access throughout the home. While construction is never invisible, careful planning helps keep the process manageable.

If you’re considering a remodeling project or home addition and want to understand your options, our team is happy to talk through scope, timing, and next steps. Thoughtful planning is the foundation of a successful project, and we’re here to help guide that process.

Choosing a Contractor
How do I choose a remodeling contractor?

The best contractors get work through satisfied customers’ referrals not from the biggest ads in the paper. Consult friends and neighbors who have had work done and ask for a referral.

Also consult the Better Business Bureau and Angie’s List for reviews of the contractors you’re considering. Be wary of a contractor with more than two or three negative reviews or complaints.

Ensure that your contractor is licensed. Licensing won’t guarantee success, but it does indicate a degree of professionalism and suggests that the contractor is committed to his or her job. The same holds true for membership in, or certification by, an industry group such as the National Association of the Remodeling Industry (NARI) and the NAHB Remodeling Council.

Ask to see a current Certificate of Insurance, so that you can see that the contractor has both General Liability and Worker’s Compensation coverage. Everyone say’s “fully insured,” but many are not.

No matter how you find potential contractors, be sure to ask for a list of previous customers that you can call for referrals. Then call them and, if possible, visit their homes to look at the work. Ask specific questions such as:

Would you hire this contractor again?
Were you satisfied with the quality of the work?
How did the contractor handle cleanup each day?
How did the contractor handle differences and work changes?
Was the job completed on time and at the bid price? If not, why not?
Were the contractors and staff knowledgeable, friendly and helpful? Were they quick to respond to any questions or concerns you may have had?

You might also ask the contractor for a list of his or her building-material suppliers. Call them to see if the contractor has an account or pays for items upon delivery. Most suppliers are willing to extend credit to financially reliable contractors.

*Attention: Federal law requires that we present you with the “Lead-Safe Certified Guide to Renovate Right”. Click here to read the booklet. Paper booklets are available upon request.

How do I spot a questionable contractor?

A warning signal should sound in your head if you encounter any of the following:

High-pressure sales tactics or threats to rescind a special price if you don’t sign on the spot.
A contractor who tries to scare you into signing a contract by claiming that your house puts you at peril (i.e., “Your electrical wiring could start a fire if it isn’t replaced.”)
A contractor who makes unsolicited phone calls or visits. Be especially wary of people who offer a bargain price, claiming that they’re doing a job in the neighborhood and have leftover materials.
A contractor whose address can’t be verified, who uses only a post office box, or who has only an answering service and no separate listing in the telephone book.
A contractor who isn’t affiliated with any recognized trade association.
License or insurance information you can’t verify.
A contractor who can’t (or won’t) provide references for similar jobs in your area.
The promise of a hefty discount—but no mention of the total cost of the job.
The promise of a deep discount if the contractor uses your home as a “demo.”

 

All contractors say “fully insured” but what does that mean?

Contractors should carry General Liability, Worker’s Compensation, NYS Disability, Vehicle and Builder’s Risk Insurances. Advertising claims are not good insurance; to be sure your contractor has current, paid-up insurance ask to see a Certificate of Insurance. These are an official statement of coverage, produced by the contractor’s insurance company. It is common for customers to ask for these and any good contractor will be able to provide one within days.

Bathrooms
Why should I choose a full service bathroom remodeler?

A full service remodeler like Bennett, will take care of all the preliminary steps involved in designing and creating your new bathroom from design and planning, to securing building codes and permits and scheduling.

Bennett’s full service remodeling will also guide you through the process of choosing the right materials for the job. Bennett partners with various local suppliers who have showrooms, samples and National Kitchen & Bath Association (NKBA) certified designers.  A bathroom may be small, but it includes many choices:

Plumbing fixtures, tub, sink, faucet and accessories
Cabinets, mirrors, countertops
Design & install of tile, marble and ceramic materials
Shower door installation
Lighting & heating design
Painting, wainscoting and wall paper design

With 100 years of experience, and thousands of completed jobs from handicap accessible to custom spa designs, Bennett can advise you each step of the way. Our licensed plumbers and electricians on staff work efficiently, meeting all the local codes and inspector requirements.

What are the pros and cons of acrylic bath liners?

The Advantages

1. Buying an acrylic bathtub liner and surround is easy. You can find lots of companies that will install an acrylic bathtub liner in your bathroom.

2. No demolition necessary if you choose an acrylic bathtub liner. This is the leading reason for having an acrylic bathtub liner and surround installed. The liner goes in the old tub.

3. The actual installation can be completely done in one day. On the other hand, replacing a bathtub and remodeling your bathroom can take several days.

The Disadvantages

1. A tub liner hides the problems, but doesn’t solve them. Water damaged walls, mold, rusty pipes, slow drains, inadequate wiring, get covered up by the liner and lots of caulk.

2. An acrylic bathtub is narrower and the sides are higher. Since it’s a tub in a tub, acrylic bathtub liners make your original tub two or three inches narrower and higher which makes it harder to reach into. It’s more difficult to clean the tub, bathe the kids, hand wash clothing, etc.

3. When you are done, it’s the “same old bathroom”. If your goal is to improve your overall bathroom appearance, create a safer, cleaner more comfortable place with better lighting, tile floors, shower seats, grab bars, big mirrors, warm floors and more then a simple acrylic liner may not be the right choice.

Conclusion

If you are looking for a “quick fix” the tub insert is quick and easy. If you want 20 years of quality and comfort in a newly designed bathroom then consider a remodel that will redesign layouts, update fixtures, replace the plumbing and wiring if needed and create a whole new bathroom experience. Contact a full service bathroom expert like Bennett Contracting for a free consultation.

Kitchens
What should I expect from a quality kitchen contractor?

When you choose a full service remodeler like Bennett, all the steps involved in creating your new kitchen from design and planning to building code and installation requirements, are professionally handled by experienced project managers and contractors. Bennett’s design/build process will guide you through the steps of choosing the right design and materials to create your desired kitchen. Bennett partners with various local suppliers who have showrooms, samples and National Kitchen & Bath Association (NKBA) certified designers. Your kitchen is the heartbeat of your home; it needs to be both beautiful and functional. Here are some of things to look for when considering a contractor to remodel your kitchen:

Architectural plans when a remodel involves structural changes or enlarging the home
NKBA certified kitchen designer, with full CAD drawings of the layout and cabinetry
Plumbing fixture showroom accessibility for selecting fixtures, sink, faucet and accessories
Wide choice of cabinets, countertops and flooring
Tile, marble, ceramic designs and installation
Lighting design services
Full line of appliances and installation

With 100 years of experience, and thousands of completed jobs from handicap accessible to custom chef’s kitchens, Bennett can advise you each step of the way. Our licensed plumbers and electricians on staff work efficiently, meeting all the local codes and inspector requirements.

Porches & Decks
My front porch is in poor condition, what should I do?

Porches are complicated structures and their design is governed by a wide variety of codes and safety standards. Refer to the “how to select a contractor” section and then call a professional full service contractor like Bennett to set up a free consultation in order to identify what issues need to be addressed.

Porches in disrepair can pose risk and hazard to the homeowner and should not be ignored.
Many times older porches were built with inadequate footings, resulting in settling or sagging of the structure.
In certain cases where the roof is in good condition, the porch roof can be braced while new footings, columns, framing and decking are rebuilt below.
Wood rot is a very common problem with porches since they are exposed to the elements. This rot can result in a danger to the integrity of the structure.
The longer you neglect to repair or rebuild a porch, the worse the problem will get.
What Material should I select for my Deck Surface and Railings?

A deck’s structural framing is constructed with pressure-treated framing lumber and sits on steel or concrete piers.

The area of the deck that you walk on and the railings are available in a variety of materials including several grades and species of wood, modern composites and PVC (vinyl). Second only to the size of the deck, the choice of material will have the most effect on the purchase cost and future maintenance requirements.

Wood:

Pressure treated wood (southern yellow pine most common)
Available in standard (lower cost) and select grades (less knots)
Premium Species including Cedar, Mahogany and Teak
Higher cost, longer lasting, better looking.
All wood is higher maintenance. It is recommended to paint or stain the surface annually

Composite:

High cost, low maintenance
Wide variety of colors, and surfaces

PVC (vinyl)

High cost
Very low maintenance
Limited colors

A full service contractor like Bennett Contracting will help you design and create your ideal outside space while keeping in mind your budgetary restrictions.

Siding
Why Choose Vinyl Siding?

Beauty

While traditional pastel and earthy color options are still available, today’s vinyl siding offers a comprehensive array of darker color combinations including bold, rich tones like barn reds, hunter and sage greens, deep blues and more. Nearly 350 different colors are certified to meet the ASTM (American Society for Testing and Materials) standards for vinyl siding color retention, so you can be sure the shades you select will resist major color changes in a variety of climates.

Durability

Of course exterior cladding has to look good for today’s discerning homeowners, but it also has a vitally important job of protecting a home from the elements. With the ability to withstand high winds (certified up to 110 mph or higher) and a composition that resists heat, cold and moisture, vinyl siding retains its great looks over time.

Vinyl siding never needs paint. Ever. The only maintenance it will need is a simple wash with a soft cloth and garden hose to keep it looking great, a feature today’s strapped-for-time homeowners really appreciate!

Green Building

Today’s vinyl siding, the most popular choice for exterior cladding in the United States and Canada, delivers recognized environmental benefits to help make and keep homes green.

Throughout the processes of manufacturing, transportation, installation, service life and waste management, vinyl siding scores well on tough environmental measures.  What’s more, vinyl siding has the potential to contribute to achieving more points than other exterior cladding in the leading green building certification programs including the United States Green Building Council (USGBC) LEED® for New Construction and LEED® Homes Rating Systems and the ANSI approved ICC 700-2008 National Green Building Standard™.

Choice

Any look – historic to contemporary – can be achieved with today’s vinyl siding. Vinyl siding has the widest array of profile offerings of any other cladding material including:

Horizontal and vertical panels
Shakes, Scallops, Shingles, Fish scales
Traditional lap
Dutch lap
Beaded designs in various profile widths

Today’s vinyl siding is available in a broad and ever increasing spectrum of solid and variegated colors. Dozens of new trim and accent options are also available to enhance neighborhood aesthetics. Vinyl siding is the number one choice for siding and Certain-Teed is the number one brand of siding.

How do I choose the right siding contractor?

One of the most important decisions you can make when it comes to fixing the exterior of your home is to hire a reputable siding company, like Bennett Contracting. While it might be tempting to take this project on by yourself, using a quality siding contractor can assure that your building products are installed correctly, avoiding any problems in the future from incorrect installation. To ensure you have a qualified siding installer, look for the following qualifications:

Certification: 

Your siding contractor should have skilled installers who have been trained by the manufacturer of the siding for your home.  Bennett employees are dual certified both be the Vinyl Siding Institute and Certain-Teed’s Five Star program. Beware of contractors who subcontract the installation.

Safety:

Your siding contractor should have the latest OSHA approved scaffolding and ladders, modern trucks and employees who have completed both OSHA safety and EPA Lead Safe Work Practice training. Your siding contractor should show you proof of insurances including worker’s compensation. Ask to see a certificate.

Choices, Designs, Referrals:

A quality siding contractor, like Bennett Contracting, has been around a long time and has hundreds of satisfied customers and completed homes like yours that you can look at.  You should also be able to view a computer rendering of your home to sample design choices. Look for siding contractor who offers options.  Insulation choices, such as blow-in cellulose, can make tremendous difference in your utility bills.

See How to choose a remodeling contractor for more general information.

How do I clean my vinyl siding?

How do I wash vinyl siding?
Wash vinyl siding with a soft cloth or ordinary long-handled, soft bristle brush. For textured surfaces, use only a soft bristle brush to keep the grooves in the texture stain-free. For best results, start at the bottom of the house and work up and rinse the cleaning solution completely before it dries.

Can I use a power washer?
Yes, though you should read the washer instructions carefully before use. When cleaning, hold the power washer straight at eye level to keep the water on top of the siding where it can clean most effectively. Do not aim the power washer upward as water may be driven behind the siding. Use caution around any opening in the wall, such as windows, doors, electrical wiring, and plumbing.

How do I remove mold and mildew?
Small spots of mold and mildew can be handled with cleaners such as Fantastik® or Windex®. For larger sections, a solution of vinegar (30%) and water (70%) has proven successful. Alternatively, you also could try the following solution: 1/3 cup (2 2/3 ounces) powdered laundry detergent (e.g., Tide®, Fab®, or equivalent), 2/3 cup (5 1/3 ounces) powdered household cleaner (e.g., Spic & Span®, Soilax®, or equivalent), 1 quart (32 fluid ounces) liquid laundry bleach, and 1 gallon (128 fluid ounces) of water.

What types of cleaners should I use for other stains?

After removing the stain, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not use cleaners containing organic solvents, undiluted chlorine bleach, liquid grease remover, nail polish remover, or furniture polish or cleaners. They can affect the surface of the siding.

WINDOWS/DOORS
How do I choose a quality window and door contractor?

Picking a high quality window is important. It helps ensure energy efficiency and insulation for your home.  Picking a high quality and experienced window installer is essential. High efficiency windows will not perform as designed unless they are correctly installed. Don’t be tempted to simply pick the contractor with the lowest price. The money you invested in the window could be wasted if they are not correctly installed.

Choices/Referrals

A full service window contractor will offer all types of windows and doors; wood, vinyl and metal from several manufacturers, to be able to select the product that best compliments your home. Beware of “one-size fits all” window companies who only sell one brand.
You should expect your contractor to have a fixed business location with a showroom, warehouse and service department.
Quality window contractors have been around a long time and will have many satisfied customers and homes like yours that you can go look at.
Windows and doors are components of your home and your installer should be versatile with carpentry skills and knowledge of construction.

Skills/Warrantee

A quality window installer has ongoing training programs or their employees and is certified by several window manufacturers.
Quality trades people are NOT piece-rate paid subs, they are hourly employees of an established local business.
You should receive two written warrantees, one from the installer for labor and one from the manufacturer covering the product.
Keep in mind that lifetime warrantees from companies that have only been in business a few years and not worth very much.

Safety

Your window contractor should have the latest OSHA approved scaffolding and ladders, modern trucks and employees who have completed both OSHA safety and EPA Lead Safe Work Practice training. Your window contractor should also show you proof of insurance, including worker’s compensation.  Ask to see a certificate.

See How to choose a remodeling contractor for more general information.

What type of material should I select for my replacement window?

Today’s windows are made of a combination of materials but generally fall into one of three categories: vinyl, wood or metal. Vinyl and wood are the two most popular for use in residential homes. What you are seeking from your windows in terms of budget, maintenance, look and function will help determine which style is right for your home.

Vinyl

Vinyl windows are the most popular because they are less costly, are available in many styles and require very little maintenance.
Vinyl windows are available in several forms:  double hung, casement, bay or bow, slider, garden, hopper and picture.
Bennett’s vinyl windows are manufactured in the Northeast from American made components.
All of the vinyl windows offered by Bennett Contracting come with a lifetime warrantee.

Wood

Wood windows are popular for their authentic look and feel. In historic areas wood is required, but in many older homes it’s just the right choice.
Wood windows are available with a low maintenance metal or vinyl cladding on the exterior.
Wood windows are available in a variety of woods including oak and pine for interior finishes.
Wood windows are available in several styles including: double hung, casement, bay, bow, hopper and picture.

Choices/Referrals:

A full service window contractor will offer all types of windows and doors including wood, vinyl and metal, from several manufacturers, to provide you with a selection of products that best compliments your home.
Beware of “one-size fits all” window companies who only sell one brand.
Quality window contractors have been around a long time and will have many satisfied customers and homes like yours that you can go look at.
Windows and doors are components of your home and your installer should be versatile with carpentry skills and knowledge of construction.
What Is A Change Order

Change Orders (CO’s) are the means by which we add, delete or modify the Work Schedule.

The Change Order form details the change in scope and the change in cost.

Here are some tips about change orders:

 

It’s OK: Don’t be scared of CO’s, they are normal and it is our way of documenting changes. It is very common for a project to have at least one change order. Larger jobs may have multiple change orders throughout the project’s duration.

 

Allowances: A specified dollar amount included in the price, which is how we budget for those materials that you need to select (ie tile). If you spend more than your allowance, the difference will be added plus sales tax. If you spend less, we credit the difference.

 

Adding: If you want to add work, just ask!!! The earlier the better, that way we can determine the impact on the job. It can be very cost effective to have our crew provide some added work while we’re already at your home working.

 

Modifications: Altering work can be tricky. If we’ve already ordered material based upon the original contract, and you request modifications, certain items may not be returnable. Also, if we have to re-do work that you’ve decided to change, we still need to charge for the labor and materials to do it again.

 

Time Frame: Adding or modifying work will result in the job taking longer. In some cases, if we have to wait for materials to arrive, we may even need to pull the crew off until the materials arrive and we can get back to work. Be prepared for these delays. Some Change Orders are out of our control and are just plain necessary.
Rot/Repairs: If we discover rot, it is necessary to fix it now. We will not ignore or cover up rot…it will only get worse and cost more down the road.
Code Upgrades: Most commonly with plumbing and electrical and especially in older homes. We always intend to include observable code upgrades, but we may discover hidden code violations inside the wall that require upgrades.
Surprise! Occasionally, we discover an unforeseen problem on a job. Maybe a cracked beam that was hidden. Be prepared for surprises.

 

Identify:  If possible, do a quick review with the Lead Carpenter each day.  If you would like to add work or make any modifications, first discuss with the Lead Carpenter to confirm if the change is possible and what might be involved. If necessary, the Project Manager or Designer will become involved with larger modifications.  Your Lead Carpenter may come to you with proposed changes (ie rot is discovered).

 

Communicating:  Once identified, in order to proceed, our Lead Carpenter will need your written or verbal authorization to do that additional work.  Be aware that if you agree to have additional work done, you are agreeing to pay for that work.  The Lead Carpenter will not offer to do extra work for free. Details of the added costs will be drawn up on a CO form for your review, either before the work is started or after (if Time & Material is used).

 

Pricing:  CO’s are either priced based upon Time & Material, or Lump Sum.  Either way, the price is determined based on materials, labor, subcontractors, taxes plus overhead and profit.  The rates and mark up percentages are spelled out on the Work Schedule.  The Project Manager and the Owner will determine which is used.

 

Conclusion:  You and Bennett are working together to create the project that you have imagined. We both want your job completed quickly, safely and with the best possible outcome.  In order to do that, we want to work with you in a collaborative manner. If changes are needed to reach that goal, we will work together to make that happen.

We added a new bathroom. GARRETT WAS OUTSTANDING!! He was prompt, courteous, his ability to create everything was amazing. There was no job GARRETT couldn't handle. Congratulations to Bennett for hiring such an outstanding and honest individual. GARRETT IS TRULY THE BEST!

Bennett Contracting replaced all of our windows and installed a sliding glass door about a year and a half ago.  They also took another sliding glass door out and put in a window as well as a wall where it was. It was a great experience.  They have excellent workmanship.  I would recommend them to anyone.  It was a good price and a lot less than some other groups that we had estimates from.  They were very nice to deal with and I will call them again.  They were great.

Put vinyl siding on detached 2-car garage.   Repaired/replaced a few dented pieces on existing aluminum siding on house.  Responded quickly to request for estimate.   Estimator very professional.  Took a few days for the estimate but the estimate was professionally done and the lowest estimate we received.   Other companies who gave us an estimate gave us an estimate on the spot but they were obviously "ball park" type estimates on their part and were higher than Bennett's. Bennett was able to do some trim work that other companies said couldn't be done (at least not by them).   They arrived on time and completed the work quickly to our satisfaction.   We understood that the estimate did not include costs of "lead paint safety" issues (a new law), and we did question the amount of those costs when they were added, but Bennett worked with us on that issue and it was satisfactorily resolved.

We needed to repair a 2-story back porch on a two family house.  Bennett came and reviewed what needed to be done and recommended that we replace everything.  We agreed that made the most sense and contracted with the company to replace the back porches.  It went extremely well.  We were originally planning to have the work done in late August or September.  Kevin called us and said they had an opening in their schedule if we wanted it done sooner.  We had the work done in July and it couldn't be better.  Not only do the porches look good, the materials are maintenance free and we won't have to worry about the porches again.  They were responsive to my concerns and made suggestions to make the project go smoothly.  Kevin was very good to work with and the carpenters were terrific - clean, professional, and easy to work with.  The site was cleaned up every day.  Everyone was pleasant and kept us informed each day of their progress.  We couldn’t be happier and will certainly use this company again.

Had a large deck installed by Bennett and we were completely satisfied with the work. The estimator did a great job taking in our ideas and added a few of his own. We chose composite decking material and we were completely satisfied with the outcome. We've had Bennett do other jobs for us and we experience the same level of superb craftsmanship each time. Highly recommend. Good experience working with these folks.

Contacted several contractors for an estimate on siding and gutters for our addition. Bennett had the best price, took the time to explain our options and made the process as easy as possible. Finished product still looks great a year out. Would definitely turn to them for future projects.

Hi guys, yes, we have used your fantastic company to add on an addition to our home. You had the whole job done in less than two months. Your guys were there everyday and the finished product was gorgeous! We only trust Bennett with our home. Thank you again for a job well done!

So ... Bennett just wrapped up a project at our home East of Albany. What started out as a possible siding job wound up as a complete window replacement, siding and roof replacement job and... minor bathroom renovation. Throughout the process, from the initial visit with Kevin Gutman to the men on site, the experience was a positive one. I strongly recommend Bennett for all of your renovation needs - Just started a fund for what I hope to be phase two come spring!

We just used Bennett for the first time to replace some fairly large windows my husband couldn't do himself. I am very impressed. We had gotten a few estimates and these guys seemed to have the best product for the best price. We also loved that the sales guy was in & out of our house unlike some other ones that stayed here for over an hour trying to sell us everything under the moon. The windows were put in yesterday & I can't believe how quick they were. The contractors were professional & skillful. If I ever need anything else done to the house I would call them again for sure.

We were in the process of having our bathroom re-done by Bennett when Hurricane Irene came along and complicated things by flooding our basement and leaving us without power. We were so impressed with the work John was doing on the bathroom, that we immediately called Bennett to arrange for them to take care of the damaged basement. The happy ending to the story is that both jobs came out beautifully!

Our estimator/project mgr Steve did a very good job explaining the process and giving a fair estimate.  He was there every step of the way to make sure I was happy with the work.  They moved patio doors from Kitchen to Dining room.  Walled up kitchen with new window and took down old porch off kitchen and put up new deck. The guys who did the work did a great job of getting to the house early every day.  They were able to answer every 'annoying homeowner' question and concern with no problems or judgment.  The job took a little over two weeks.  The workmanship on the deck was wonderful.  Every edge was routed down.  I haven't gotten to use it yet since it's been cold but it looks great!  They cleaned up everything and no detail was left untouched.  They even fixed the spring on my garage door (at no charge) that happened to break while they were working.  I'd definitely use them again.

Bennett Contracting provided estimate in June 2011 and then did work in September, working around my schedule. One carpenter, John, did most of the work including installation of the floor tile.  John brought in Bennett's plumber and electrician as needed.  Everything went smoothly from start to finish and consistent with the work schedule provided in June.  I was consulted when necessary and any questions I had as the work progressed were graciously answered.   All I can say is that everyone did the job asked of them and did it well.  Without exception they were all pleasant to deal with and performed professionally.  I would definitely hire them again.

We had siding put on the house by Bennett Contracting. He was here in September and they did the whole job in 2 weeks. They do all kinds of things. They were very good. There were here for 2 weeks and when they were here they were working and there was no fooling around. We got estimates from several places and that estimate was good. They were very punctual. They came everyday at the time they said they would and they worked all day. I think they were very professional. They had a supervisor who was there all the time. There were 3 guys and 1 guy was in charge and they took their lead from him.

Removed a fireplace and replaced it with a wall of windows; replaced a sliding patio door with french doors; replaced two leaky skylights with two ceiling windows; repaired roof; repaired siding; repaired gutter and downspout; installed additional vents in eaves for attic circulation. This was a story of persistence and ultimate success. Some snafus in the ordering process caused some delays, but overall the crew and management were fastidious in their attention to detail and quality.
